supporting_observations.claim: At 13:48:08 UTC, a Windows event recorded a PowerShell process on WS-KNGUYEN-01, running as SYSTEM, supplying explicit credentials for svc-routes to access FILE-COP-01.
The event is not a failed-logon event and, by itself, does not show whether authentication succeeded or whether there were repeated failures.

The source workstation differs from the documented workstation used for remote administration, while the scheduled svc-routes password rotation provides a possible benign context; neither fact establishes whether this credential use was authorized.

known_telemetry_limitations: Only one log record is available for the review window.
The supplied record logs explicit credential use but does not provide the authentication outcome or explain why the credentials were used.
No accompanying failed- or successful-logon events, process details beyond the recorded executable, or activity from the service job are provided.
claims_not_established: That repeated failed domain logons for svc-routes occurred around 13:40 UTC.
That the credential attempt succeeded or failed.
That the PowerShell activity was authorized password-rotation work or malicious credential use.
Who initiated or controlled the process running as SYSTEM.
additional_evidence_needed: Domain-controller authentication records for svc-routes and FILE-COP-01 from 13:20 to 14:20 UTC, including success and failure events.
Process creation and PowerShell logging from WS-KNGUYEN-01 around 13:48 UTC, including command line, parent process, and initiating user.
Change or job-update records showing who rotated the svc-routes password and whether RouteSync was updated.
Relevant FILE-COP-01 logs showing RouteSync executions and authentication results during the review window.
